Miko Targeting Guide
https://en.touhouwiki.net/wiki/Toyosatomimi_no_Miko

Toyosatomimi no Miko is a character from the Touhou Project series of bullet hell (and fighting) games, and the main antagonist of Touhou 13: Ten Desires.

Backstory
- Miko is Crown Prince Shoutoku (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Sh%C5%8Dtoku), a semi-legendary regent of medieval Japan. Prince Shoutoku is famous for uniting and modernize a realm previously ruled by feudal warlords. He made Buddhism the official state religion, wrote the first constitution, instituted government reforms, and has been depicted on the front of Yen banknotes.
- According to Touhou lore, promoting Buddhism was just a front to pacify the population. In secret, Miko practiced Taoist magic to become immortal. She transformed her body into a sacred sword and her sword into a new immortal body. Her acolytes did the same with other vessels. She slept in her mausoleum, awaiting her resurrection. Eventually, because people IRL started questioning if Prince Shoutoku ever actually existed, her mausoleum ended up in Gensokyo, the “land of illusion/dreams” and setting of Touhou. She eventually woke up because a bunch of buddhist parked a flying ship/temple on top of her.
- You may have noticed that despite Prince Shotoku being a man, Miko is a woman. Touhou never delves deep into this discrepancy, allowing instead for fan theories. These range from “She was always a woman and everyone forgot somehow” to “:transgender_flag:”. I go with the “Fate” explanation: she was always a woman, but hid her gender using magic so she could rule unquestioned.
- Miko is accompanied by her consort, Soga no Tojiko. Tojiko is based on (one of) Prince Shoutoku’s historical consorts, Tojiko no Iratsume, daughter of Soga no Umako and Mononobe no Futso-hime. In Touhou lore, she was one of Miko’s vassals who studied Taoism and attempted to become immortal. But because the vase she attempted to transform into her body was sbotaged by her fellow vassal Mononobe no Futo, she wound up as a vengeful spirit. She also has thunder powers. Despite all that, she’s chill.
- Miko’s backstory is nothing special by Touhou standards.

Personality
- Miko is arrogant and elitist, but backs it up with intelligence, wit, wisdom, and power. There’s a reason that, in a series populated by smug jerks, Miko is noted to be particularly smug.
- Miko is a womanizer and a lesbian. She thinks she’s god’s gift to women (but she also thinks she’s god’s gift to humanity). Despite this, she’s not a selfish lover, and will treat any sexual partner right.
- While she can be pragmatic and politically astute, she’s usually easygoing, which may be surprising considering her station. She’s particularly at home in a game like this, where she can both ogle women and be the center of attention.
- Despite being a noblewoman, Tojiko is rough around the edges. Most of her ire is directed toward her prince, though, and she’s friendly to people who *don’t* annoy her. She’s still fiercely loyal to Miko, though Tojiko sees her for who she truly is. Feel free to target her as much as the Crown Prince.

*hings Worth Targeting
- Miko loves talking about herself, her reign as regent of Japan, her current role as head of Gensokyo’s Taoist clan, and politics and history in general.
- Miko is accompanied by a ghost attendant who’s also her wife, Tojiko. Tojiko strips Miko, who she calls *the Crown Prince*, and “takes care of her” during the forfeit. She pops in whenever she’s needed.
- Miko loves the ladies. Expect her to proposition large chested characters.
- Miko radiates confidence, but acts casual. She’s willing to give out political, romantic, or sexual advise, if your character wants it.
- Miko has a prompt marker, where she asks her tablemates to reveal their most inner desire.
- Miko thinks she better than you. And she’s right.
